<execute-bead>
  <instructions>
You are executing one bead inside an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the completion contract — every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file you can point to after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

The bead is too big when any of these holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs as separate top-level deliverables.
- Description names multiple feature-sized sub-pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across more than ~5 files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, treat Step 0 as a split-first pass and favor child-bead scoping before implementation.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, decomposed children may split once more, and third-level splits must be rejected with an explanation.

If too big, decompose — do not attempt the work:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child slice (focused title, description, AC; copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'` so the decomposition is visible.
4. Write `.ddx/executions/20260507T000923-657c0c98/no_changes_rationale.txt` listing each child ID and slice, then stop.

A clean decomposition is a successful attempt. Do not mix partial implementation with decomposition.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC against concrete evidence (test name, file path, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- If you cannot finish, write `.ddx/executions/20260507T000923-657c0c98/no_changes_rationale.txt` (what is done, what blocks, what a follow-up needs) before exiting. No commit and no rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`. A well-justified no_changes beats a bad commit.

## no_changes contract

If you write `.ddx/executions/20260507T000923-657c0c98/no_changes_rationale.txt`, it MUST carry one of:

- `verification_command: <one-line shell command>` — the loop runs it (cwd = project root, 60s); exit 0 closes the bead, non-zero rejects.
- `status: needs_investigation` + `reason: <why>` — bead stays open for triage.

Bare rationales ("nothing to do") are rejected.

## Reports

Freestanding artifacts (investigation reports, findings docs) go under `.ddx/executions/20260507T000923-657c0c98/` (the per-attempt evidence directory under `.ddx/executions/`). **Never write reports to `/tmp` or any path outside the repository** — out-of-repo paths are invisible to the post-merge reviewer and cause BLOCK on missing evidence. If the bead names a specific in-repo path, use it; else default to `.ddx/executions/20260507T000923-657c0c98/<short-name>.md`. Stage and commit the report alongside code.

## Bead overrides project defaults

The bead description and AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and conservative project defaults (YAGNI, DOWITYTD, no-docs-unless-asked) in this worktree — write whatever the bead asks for.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized; running it corrupts the bead queue.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other project-instructions files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator — do not keep exploring or testing.
  </instructions>
  <bead id="fizeau-83b7cc1f">
    <title>Fix session logger close race for final override events</title>
    <description>
PROBLEM
A completed Fizeau/DDx run can print a warning after the agent succeeds:

WARN session logger: write error err="write .ddx/agent-logs/svc-1778103547795097343.jsonl: file already closed"

The observed run completed its command_execution, created detached-HEAD commit 50ba08b, and produced a final response. The warning is post-run session-log persistence noise, but it can also mean a late routing-quality override event was not persisted to the per-session JSONL log. That weakens UsageReport/routing-quality reconstruction even though the user-visible execution succeeded.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
service_session_log.go:34 opens the service-owned session logger and service_session_log.go:91 writes terminal session.end events through the same logger. service_execute.go:423 defers final write/close from the runExecute goroutine and service_execute.go:436 closes the logger as soon as runExecute unwinds. service_taillog.go:153 handles final-event fanout and service_taillog.go:163 writes an override event to the same serviceSessionLog from the fanout goroutine immediately before forwarding the final event. That fanout write can race with runExecute closing the logger. internal/session/logger.go:93 closes the underlying file, but internal/session/logger.go:97-100 leaves l.file non-nil, so any late Write reaches internal/session/logger.go:85 and logs "session logger: write error" against a closed file.

PROPOSED FIX
Make service session-log ownership deterministic so all session-log events that belong to an Execute call are persisted before the logger is closed. Prefer moving or synchronizing override-event persistence so the final-event fanout cannot write to a logger after runExecute closes it. Add a defensive logger close behavior only if it complements, rather than hides, the ordering fix: Logger.Close may set l.file nil after close, but the regression test must still prove the override event is persisted, not silently dropped.

In-scope files:
- service_execute.go
- service_taillog.go
- service_session_log.go
- internal/session/logger.go
- focused tests in service_*_test.go and/or internal/session/logger_test.go

NON-SCOPE
Do not change the public Execute event schema, harness-native stream parsers, benchmark matrix reporting, DDx CLI behavior, or TerminalBench/FHI logic. Do not suppress the warning without preserving the late override/routing-quality session-log event.

PARENT AND DEPENDENCIES
Parent: fizeau-06524f43. Dependencies: none.
    </description>
    <acceptance>
1. Add a regression test named TestExecuteSessionLogOverrideEventPersistsBeforeClose (or an equivalently specific Test* name) that exercises an Execute request with override axes and SessionLogDir, drains the returned event stream, then reads the session JSONL and asserts session.start, override, and session.end records are present in deterministic order or otherwise all present without a write-to-closed-file warning.
2. Add or update a focused logger lifecycle test named TestLoggerClosePreventsLateClosedFileWriteWarning (or equivalent) only if Logger.Close behavior changes; the test must verify a late Write after Close does not attempt to write to a closed *os.File.
3. The fix preserves one terminal final event on the public Execute stream and does not drop override events from TailSessionLog subscribers.
4. The warning string "session logger: write error" is not emitted in the regression path; tests should capture slog output or otherwise prove the closed-file path is not reached.
5. go test ./... passes.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
    </acceptance>
    <notes>
Cleared stale execute-loop failure from the pre-v0.10.11 config parser error: grendel-rapid-mlx used type rapid-mlx before Fizeau accepted that provider type. Historical execution events are retained; queue eligibility should now be governed by status and dependencies.
    </notes>

data.output:
Implemented the session-log race fix, but I did not commit because the repo-wide Go suite is still red on two unrelated root-package route-resolution tests.

What changed:
- Moved override-event persistence into the execution-owned session-log path before logger close in [`service_execute.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-83b7cc1f-20260507T000923-657c0c98/service_execute.go).
- Removed the session-log write from the final-event fan-out goroutine in [`service_taillog.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-83b7cc1f-20260507T000923-657c0c98/service_taillog.go).
- Made `Logger.Close` nil out the file handle after closing in [`internal/session/logger.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-83b7cc1f-20260507T000923-657c0c98/internal/session/logger.go).
- Added the requested regression test in [`service_override_test.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-83b7cc1f-20260507T000923-657c0c98/service_override_test.go).
- Added the logger lifecycle test in [`internal/session/logger_test.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-83b7cc1f-20260507T000923-657c0c98/internal/session/logger_test.go).

Verified green:
- `go test . -run TestExecuteSessionLogOverrideEventPersistsBeforeClose -v`
- `go test ./internal/session -run TestLoggerClosePreventsLateClosedFileWriteWarning -v`

Blocked on:
- `go test ./...` fails in unrelated tests:
  - `service_route_attempts_test.go:238`
  - `service_route_attempts_test.go:416`

I recorded the blocker in:
- [no_changes_rationale.txt](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-83b7cc1f-20260507T000923-657c0c98/.ddx/executions/20260507T000923-657c0c98/no_changes_rationale.txt)

Next step:
1. Investigate the two root-package route-resolution failures so the full suite can go green and the bead can be committed.
